clauses.reason: The operative paragraphs say the President does "do hereby adopt and approve the said report, recommendation and findings of the National Industrial Recovery Board", orders "Do Hereby Order that the Code of Fair Competition for the Paper and Pulp Industry be and the same is hereby amended to the extent set forth in Schedule A attached hereto and hereby made a part hereof", and orders "Do Hereby Order that said amendment be and it is hereby approved, and that the previous approval of said Code is hereby amended to include an approval of said Code in its entirety as amended". These are section 3(a) approvals and amendments of the code with no stated period or condition. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113) repealed the provisions of Title I delegating power to the President to "approve or prescribe codes of fair competition" and "providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed"; the resolution states no effective date other than its approval ("Approved, June 14, 1935."), so the approval stopped operating on June 14, 1935. Under section 3 of Title I (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA3) an approved code had legal effect only through 3(b) standards of fair competition, 3(c) injunctions and 3(f) misdemeanor penalties, all of which the repeal removed. Schechter (SUPPLEMENT:SCHECHTERJDG, May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date, and June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936.

Under section 3 of Title I (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA3) an approved code had legal effect only through 3(b) standards of fair competition, 3(c) injunctions and 3(f) misdemeanor penalties, all of which the repeal removed. Schechter (SUPPLEMENT:SCHECHTERJDG, May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date, and June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936.

research_rationale:
Identity and page check: the held text for EO 6964B is the American Presidency Project transcription (APP node 362635), registered as grade mirror_transcription (not an original). Its page record is a Common Crawl capture of 2025-10-06T02:30:50Z whose heading names Executive Order 6964B, whose date (February 5, 1935) and subject agree with the text, and whose text sha256 equals the held text's. The WPA 1944 list row (1935 Feb 5 p.603: * Amendment to Code of Fair Competition for the Paper and Pulp Industry approved. XXI NRA Codes 271. * Does not have form of a proclamation.) confirms the order's date and subject. The order approves a code of fair competition under section 3(a) of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, so the reviewed shared analysis (SHARED_ANALYSIS.md and review-shared/ADJUDICATION.json) applies: a code-dependent command that did not end earlier ended on June 14, 1935 by statutory repeal (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2); Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date. The machine inventory omitted the adoption of the report (chars 409-1196) and split Schedule A into nine overlapping or duplicated clauses; it is corrected into three clauses: the adoption, amendment and approval paragraph, the replacement of Article V section 1, and the replacement of Article V section 5. The order amends and re-approves the code approved on November 17, 1933 (EO 6437).

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved Code of Fair Competition for the Paper and Pulp Industry before June 14, 1935 are accrued consequences that the repeal did not turn into continuing commands; nothing in S.J. Res. 113 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113) continues the approval after June 14, 1935. Any antitrust exemption for complying action before the repeal (NIRA section 5, SUPPLEMENT:NIRA5) is likewise an accrued effect; the resolution's proviso, which extends the exemption only to "agreements and action thereunder" meeting stated conditions, leaves open how far it narrowed the exemption for past action, so the claim records no continuing exemption and no surviving approval. Wages paid and acts done under the amended wage provisions before the repeal are accrued.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: A. L. A. Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, 295 U.S. 495, decided May 27, 1935: the Court held the section 3 code-making delegation unconstitutional and the Live Poultry Code provisions in question invalid. Recorded as a validity characterization for every section 3 code approval, not as this order's end; the judgment did not cancel or withdraw this order.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: enactment date of NIRA section 3; the provisions described were repealed on June 14, 1935 (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2).
source_notes.reason: NIRA section 3 (48 Stat. 195, June 16, 1933): under 3(a) the President approved codes and could impose conditions of approval; under 3(b), 3(c) and 3(f) an approved code's provisions became standards of fair competition enforceable by injunction and as misdemeanors. These are the legal effects that section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: enactment date of NIRA section 5; S.J. Res. 113 (June 14, 1935) limited the exemption by proviso; the held text does not settle the proviso's effect on past action.
source_notes.reason: NIRA section 5 exempted from the antitrust laws any code approved and in effect under Title I and any complying action while Title I was in effect and for sixty days thereafter; any exemption for action taken before the repeal is an accrued effect, not continued operation of the approval.
